Critical Apparatus Removed ## Section 1. Primary Creation and Secondary Emanation (A. 17.6b–17; Br. 1.31–56; H. 27–53; Śidh. 51.3–28)
Listen to that divine narrative which liberates one from all sins—wondrous, full of many meanings, and extensive in its scriptural detail—as it is being told by me. || 1 ||
Whoever should constantly uphold this, or listen to it repeatedly, having ensured the continuity of his own lineage, is glorified in the heavenly world. || 2 ||
That which is the unmanifest cause is eternal and consists of both the existent and the non-existent;
from that Pradhāna, the Lord Puruṣa fashioned the universe. || 3 ||
Know him, O best of sages, to be Brahmā of immeasurable luster,
the creator of all beings, who is solely devoted to Nārāyaṇa.
From the Great Principle (mahat) arises the ego-sense (ahaṃkāra); from that, the elements were born;
and from the elements, the various manifestations of the elements.
Thus is the eternal creation. || 5 ||
Listen indeed as its detailed components are being proclaimed, according to my wisdom and according to what I have heard.
It increases the fame of one's ancestors! || 6 ||
The recitation of those of steadfast fame is auspicious, conducive to glory, destructive of enemies, leading to heaven, and increasing one's lifespan.
Because he purifies all meritorious deeds, he is the entire eon for the sake of purity; he is pure. || 7 ||
From the Vṛṣṇi lineage, I shall describe the unsurpassed creation of beings.
To him who is Hiraṇyagarbha, the Puruṣa, and the Lord;
to the unborn one, whose form is the Immovable (Sthāṇu).
Having paid homage to the most excellent one, the source of all creatures, I shall proclaim the unsurpassed creation of the world.
Brahmā is the creator, Hari is the protector, and Maheśvara is the destroyer;
there is no other [agent] for that creation.
At each appropriate time, as it has passed.
Then the Blessed One, the Self-Existent, desiring to create various beings, first created the waters alone; into them he cast his seed.
The waters are called *nārāḥ*, for the waters are indeed the offspring of Nara;
since they were his first place of resort (*ayana*), he is therefore remembered as Nārāyaṇa. || 11 ||
That egg, resting upon the waters, became golden-hued;
there Brahmā himself was born, for we have heard that he is the self-existent (Svayambhū). || 12 ||
The blessed Hiraṇyagarbha, having dwelt for a full year, divided that egg into two parts: heaven and earth. || 13 ||
[The fourteen worlds were arranged below and above.
Between those two halves, the Lord created space.
He established the earth floating upon the waters and the ten directions. || 14 ||

Thereupon, Prajāpati, desiring to bring forth a creation of that same nature, emitted Time, Mind, Speech, Desire, Anger, and likewise Pleasure, creating an emanation corresponding to those forms. || 15 ||
The one of great splendor created seven mind-born sons: Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha. || 16 ||
"These seven Brahmās are established as such in the Purāṇa;
they are indeed the seven born of Brahmā, whose very essence is Nārāyaṇa. || 17 ||
Then Brahmā again created Rudra, who was born from his own wrath, as well as the omnipresent Sanatkumāra, the first-born even of the former [gods]. || 18 ||
O twice-born ones, these seven and Rudra produced progeny;
thereafter, Sanatkumāra and Tejas remain with their vital energy withdrawn. || 19 ||
Of them, there were seven great lineages, divine and accompanied by hosts of gods; they were active, possessed of progeny,
and adorned by great seers.
In the beginning, he created lightning, thunderclouds, red clouds, and Indra’s bow (the rainbow), as well as birds; and indeed, he created Parjanya (the rain-god). || 21 ||
He fashioned the Ṛg-verses, the Yajus-formulas, and the Sāman-chants for the accomplishment of sacrifice;
with these the Śādhyas sacrificed to the gods—thus indeed we have heard. || 22 ||
From his mouth he generated the gods and the ancestors, and from his chest, indeed,
the humans from his generative organ.
From his hips, he created the Asuras. || 22 ||
High and low beings were born from his limbs as the Prajāpati Āpava was creating the creation of progeny. || 23 ||
When the created beings did not increase at all, then, having divided his own body into two parts, he became a male with one half. || 24 ||
With half [of himself] he became a woman; in her he procreated various offspring, and having pervaded both heaven and earth with his majesty, he remains. || 25 ||
Viṣṇu created Virāj; he, in turn, created Puruṣa from Virāj.
One should know that Puruṣa to be Manu; his period is known as a Manvantara. || 26 ||
Thus, this second [creation] of Mānasa is called the interval of Manu.
That lordly Puruṣa, Vairāja, brought forth the creation of beings. || 27 ||
The subjects of that Nārāyaṇa-emanation are likewise not born from a womb;
a man who recites this shall become long-lived, famous, blessed, and possessed of progeny. || 28 ||
Having understood this primary creation, one shall attain the destination as desired. || 29 ||

**Chapter 1: On Mixed Progeny** **Section 2: Genealogy** Thus, when the progeny had become intermingled, the Lord of Creatures (Prajāpati), who was indeed Āpava, obtained as his wife Śatarūpā, a woman not born from a womb. || 1 ||
O best of sages, while Āpava remained pervading the heavens by his own greatness, Śatarūpā was born through dharma alone. || 1 ||
Having performed austerities most difficult to practice for a hundred years,
she obtained as her husband that Puruṣa of radiant asceticism.
O brahmins, that person who is Svāyambhuva is called Manu;
his period of authority here is said to consist of seventy-one yugas. || 1 ||
From the Puruṣa Vairāja, Śatarūpā gave birth to Vīra,
Priyavrata, and Uttānapāda.
From Vīra, Kāmyā was born. || 1 ||
The excellent daughter of the progenitor Kardama was named Kāmyā.
Sūta said:
You ought to hear in brief the creation of Cākṣuṣa,
in whose lineage he was born.
The powerful Pṛthu, son of Vena;
and other lords of subjects, such as Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas. || 1 ||
And the four sons of Kāmyā were Samrāṭ, Kukṣi, Virāṭ, and Prabhu. || 16 ||
Atri, the Prajāpati, took Uttānapāda as his son;
he was indeed his adopted son, and he became a king and a Prajāpati. || 21 ||
It was given by Svāyambhuva Manu to Atri for a specific reason;
then, having reached the Manvantara...
And [the lineage] of the future Cākṣuṣa.
O twice-born ones, I shall now explain that sixth [chapter] by way of an introduction:
Sūnṛtā gave birth to four sons from Uttānapāda.
Dharma’s daughter, renowned by the name Sūnṛtā, was fair-hipped; she was born from the horse-sacrifice and was the auspicious mother of Dhruva. || 3 ||
She of the pure smile was born from Lakṣmī, the wife of Dharma;
[and she bore] Dhruva, Kīrtimant, Āyuṣmant, and likewise Vasu.
Uttānapāda begot [a son], Prajāpati begot [him] in Sūnṛtā. || 4 ||
And two daughters of pure smiles: || 4 ||
For three thousand divine years, the valiant Dhruva performed austerities without food, seeking great renown. || 5 ||
To him, the Lord Brahmā, being pleased, granted a station equal to his own,
which was indeed immovable and foremost.
The Lord of Progeny is the father of the Seven Sages. || 6 ||
And having observed his pride, supernatural power, and greatness, Uśanas, the preceptor of the gods and asuras, even sang this verse: || 7 ||
Oh, the power of his asceticism! Oh, his learning! Oh, how wonderful it is, that the Seven Sages stand today with him placed before them as their polestar! (8)
From him, Śambhu begot Śiṣṭi, Bhavya, and Dhruva;
and Succhāyā bore children to Śiṣṭi.
[He begot] five sons who were free from blemish. || 9 ||
Bṛhatī bore to Ripu these sons: Ripuñjaya, Vipra, Vṛkala, Vṛkatejas, and Cākṣuṣa.
Cākṣuṣa Manu begot [him] upon Vairaṇī, the daughter of the high-souled Prajāpati Vīraṇa, in the Puṣkariṇī lake. || 11 ||
Ten sons of great power were born to Manu by Naḍvalā,
the daughter of the Prajāpati Vairāja, who was possessed of immense heroism.
Ūru, Pūru, Śatadyumna, Tapasvin, Śatyavāk, Kavi, Agniṣṭut, Atirātra, and Śudyumna—these are the nine. (13)
And Abhimanyu was the tenth; these were the sons of the highly energetic Ūru born of Naḍvalā.
Furthermore, the daughter of Agni bore six sons of great splendor to Ūru: || 14 ||
From Aṅga were born Śumanas, Śvāti, Kratu, Aṅgiras, and Gaya;
from the body of Śunītha, indeed, Vena alone was born as his offspring. || 15 ||
Due to the misconduct of Vena, a very great wrath arose;
then, for the sake of progeny, the sages churned his right hand. || 16 ||
When Vena’s hand was churned, a great king was born.
Seeing him, the sages said: "This protector of the earth shall be named Vainya; indeed, he will gladden the subjects. He who is celebrated as Pṛthu was thus proclaimed.
Possessing great splendor, he will achieve great fame;
born as an archer clad in armor, he will seem to burn with his brilliance. || 18 ||
Then Pṛthu, the son of Vena and the first of the Kṣatriyas, protected this earth;
he was the first sovereign of the world consecrated by the Rājasūya sacrifice. || 19 ||
And from that very [cow] were born the skillful Sūta and Māgadha;
by him, O Great King, this cow was milked for the crops by that wise one.
Desiring the livelihood of all creatures, he was [honored] by the gods together with the hosts of sages,
as well as by the ancestors, the Dānavas, and the Gandharvas along with the throngs of Apsarases.
The Earth was milked by serpents, by the Puṇyajanas, as well as by plants and mountains,
each from their respective vessels.
It yielded milk according to their desires, by which they sustained their lives.
To Pṛthu were born two sons, knowers of dharma, Antardhāna and Pālina. || 23 ||
From Śikhaṇḍin, Havirdhāna was born through a miraculous manifestation;
from Havirdhāna, Dhiṣaṇā, the daughter of Agni, gave birth to six sons. || 24 ||
Prācīnabarhis, Śukra, Gaya, Kṛṣṇa, Vraja, and Ajina;
the venerable Prācīnabarhis was a great lord of progeny (Prajāpati). || 25 ||
The great king,
by whom the subjects were nourished,
[spread] kuśa grass with its tips pointing eastward from the place where the oblation is kept.
O best of the twice-born, [this occurred] upon the earth. || 26 ||
The venerable Prācīnabarhis,
who moved upon the surface of the earth,
was [superior] in strength, sacred learning, austerity, and heroism.
He was a sole ruler on earth;
his sacrificial grass (barhis) was spread with its tips pointing eastward, and for that reason he was called Prācīnabarhis. || 26 ||
The Lord took as his wife the daughter of the ocean.
At the conclusion of his great asceticism, Prajāpati begot ten sons upon Sāmudrī Savarṇā, who was the wife of Prācīnabarhis. || 28 ||
All those named Pracetas, who had reached the further shore of the science of archery,
practiced great austerity while following the path of dharma without deviation.
While the Pracetas were performing austerities, lying within the waters of the ocean for ten thousand years, trees overspread the earth.
Being left unprotected, they were overwhelmed by calamities, and then there occurred a destruction of living beings;
this happened during that period of Manu Cākṣuṣa when [the protection] had been withdrawn.
The wind was unable to blow, for the sky was covered with trees;
for ten thousand years, living beings were unable to move. || 32 ||
Having heard that, all the Pracetas, endowed with ascetic power and filled with wrath,
emitted wind and fire from their mouths.
Then, having uprooted those trees, the wind dried them up;
the terrible fire consumed them, and thus occurred the destruction of the trees. || 34 ||
Then, perceiving that the trees were inexhaustible while only a few branches remained, King Soma approached those Prajāpatis and said to them: || 35 ||
"Restrain your anger, O kings, all you descendants of Prācīnabarhis;
the earth has been stripped of its trees—let fire and wind be appeased! (36)
"By half of your splendor and by half of my own splendor, a wise one named Dakṣa, a lord of creatures (Prajāpati), shall be born from her. || 39 ||
He, being himself like fire, will further cause these subjects—who have been mostly consumed by the fire consisting of your own splendor—to flourish once more. || 40 ||
Then, at the word of Soma, those Pracetasas restrained their anger toward the trees and, in accordance with dharma, accepted Māriṣā as their wife, O noble one.
Then they indeed conceived a child in Māriṣā by means of their minds;
from the ten Pracetas, Prajāpati [was born] in Māriṣā. || 42 ||

The highly energetic and powerful Dakṣa was born from a portion of Soma; he begot sons, first creating through his mind those who would increase the lineage of Soma. Dakṣa produced progeny not through sexual union.
Having created both the immobile and the mobile— both bipeds and quadrupeds—
the skillful Dakṣa subsequently created women by means of his mind.
The Lord gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa,
and the remaining ones, known as the constellations (nakṣatras) and engaged in the guidance of time, he gave to King Soma— twenty-seven to the Moon.
Having given these [daughters] to them, he then gave four others to Ariṣṭanemi;
two to Bahuputra and likewise two to Aṅgiras; and one maiden, Kaṇyā, to Kṛśāśva. Now learn of the offspring born from them! || 45 ||
The sixth interval here is proclaimed as that of Cākṣuṣa Manu, and also that of the seventh Prajāpati, Vaivasvata Manu. || 45 ||
From them were born the gods, birds, cattle, serpents, sons of Diti and Danu, Gandharvas, Apsarases, and indeed other species. || 46 ||
From that time forward, offspring in this world were born from sexual union;
it is said that for the ancestors, creation occurred through mere intention, sight, and touch. || 47 ||
The sages (ṛṣis) said:
"The origin of the gods, the dānavas, the gandharvas, the uragas, and the rākṣasas, as well as that of the high-souled Dakṣa, has been told previously."
Brahmā was born from the thumb; O sinless one, you have stated that Prajāpati’s birth was from the vital breath (prāṇa), and you have described the birth of Dakṣa. || 49 ||
And likewise, from his left thumb, his wife was born. || 49 ||
"How did that great ascetic again obtain the state of being Prācetasa?
O Sūta, you ought to explain this doubt of ours here:
how did he, who was the grandson of Soma, become his father-in-law? (50)
(Heart-stirring) Sūta said:
"Arising and cessation occur constantly among living beings;
the seers and those people who possess knowledge are not deluded in this regard. || 51 ||
In every age, all these kings beginning with Dakṣa come into being, and they are likewise dissolved again; the wise man is not deluded by this. || 52 ||
O best of the twice-born, even among them there was previously no seniority or juniority;
austerity alone was weightier, and spiritual power was the sole cause [of distinction]. || 53 ||
Whoever knows this creation of Dakṣa, including all that is moving and unmoving,
shall be blessed with offspring, shall transcend [the span of] life, and shall be glorified in the heavenly world. || 54 ||
Thus has the creation of Cākṣuṣa been briefly described. These six creations, consisting of the Manvantaras, have indeed been recounted. (541)
O best of the twice-born, these creations, beginning with that of Svāyambhuva and ending with that of Cākṣuṣa, have been described in due order in brief by the wise. (542)
The detailed account of them should be known through the emanation of Vivasvat;
all those emanations of Vivasvat are neither deficient nor redundant. || 543 ||
He who recites this without malice attains these very qualities: a healthy lifespan according to its measure, in accordance with the Dharma, through desire, and for the sake of wealth. || 544 ||
I shall describe the creation of the high-souled Vaivasvata, who is present now;
listen as I speak of it both in brief and in detail! || 545 ||
## Section 2. Genealogy | Chapter 2.
The Sages (Ṛṣis) said:
[Please tell us] concerning the gods, the Dānavas, the Gandharvas, the Uragas, and the Rākṣasas...
O Brahmin, recount my birth in full detail! || 1 ||
Lomaharṣaṇa (the Sūta) said: Formerly, Dakṣa was commanded by the Self-born One to "create progeny.
Listen to how he created living beings.
Listen likewise, O twice-born ones! || 2 ||
In the beginning, the Lord created from his mind alone all beings:
the sages, the gods along with the gandharvas, as well as the asuras and the rākṣasas.
When the Yakṣas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, as well as birds, domestic animals, and wild beasts—which were created by her through the mind—did not increase, those creatures did not flourish. || 4 ||
Then, having reflected upon dharma for the sake of progeny, that Prajāpati, desiring to create various offspring through the practice of sexual union, [acted accordingly]. || 5 ||
He brought home Asiknī as his wife, the daughter of Vīraṇa Prajāpati, who was endowed with great ascetic merit, noble, and a savior of the worlds. || 6 ||
Then the powerful Prajāpati Dakṣa himself begot five thousand sons upon Vairiṇī and Asiknī. || 7 ||
But seeing those illustrious ones desiring to multiply their progeny,
the divine seer Nārada, whose speech is pleasant, spoke this:
The speech of those [sages] was for their own destruction and for his own curse as well—
[the curse] which Kaśyapa, the supreme lord, produced through that best of sons.
In the daughter of Dakṣa, there was a mind-born son of Kaśyapa;
due to the fear of Dakṣa’s curse, that sage [remained] under the power of Dakṣa’s curse, and therefore he [was born] from Kaśyapa.
The second was Mānasa;
for Nārada had previously arisen from Parameṣṭhin. || 10 ||
Then, O best of divine sages, he begot him once more upon Vairanī, the daughter of Asita.
Like a father, [he protected] the bull among sages. || 10 ||
Therefore, Dakṣa’s sons, renowned as the Haryaśvas, were all destroyed for the sake of dharma by fate; of this there is no doubt. || 11 ||
Then Dakṣa, of immeasurable prowess, rose up for his destruction; indeed, the Lord, being enraged, was entreated by Parameṣṭhin after placing the Brahman-sages before him. 12.
Then Dakṣa indeed made an agreement with Parameṣṭhin:
"May Nārada be born as your son from my daughter. || 13 ||
Then Dakṣa gave his beloved daughter to Parameṣṭhin;
from him that ṛṣi Nārada was born once again out of fear of the curse. || 14 ||
The sages (ṛṣis) said: "How were those sons, the offspring of Prajāpati, destroyed by the great seer Nārada? We wish to hear this according to the truth. || 15 ||
Lomaharṣaṇa (the Sūta) said: The sons of Dakṣa, the Haryaśvas, being of great prowess and desiring to increase their progeny, assembled together; Nārada then spoke to them.
Alas, you are indeed foolish;
you do not know the true extent of this earth, even as you desire to create its measure.
The subjects were the sons of Pracetas. || 17 ||
"How indeed will you create progeny within, above, and below?
Having heard those words, they departed in every direction. || 18 ||
Even now they do not cease, like rivers flowing into the oceans.
Then, when the Haryaśvas had perished, Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, [produced offspring] again.
Then the Lord begot a thousand sons upon Vairaṇī;
those Śabalāśvas then desired to increase their progeny.
But those Śabalāśvas, desiring to increase their progeny, [returned].
Urged by Nārada, they all spoke these previously mentioned words to one another: "The great sage has spoken correctly. || 21 ||
"The path of our brothers must indeed be followed; there is no doubt in this! Having ascertained the extent of the earth, we shall happily create subjects. || 22 ||
Single-minded and with tranquil minds, properly instructed, they too have departed in every direction by that very same path;
even today they do not return, like rivers into the oceans. || 23 ||
From that time on, indeed, a brother intent on searching for his brother sets out and quickly perishes; therefore, a wise person should not do such a thing.
When the Śabalāśvas had perished, the powerful Dakṣa, filled with rage, cursed Nārada: "Go to your destruction! and "May you dwell in the womb [of a woman]! || 25 ||
And having learned that those sons were lost, Dakṣa Prajāpati begot sixty daughters upon Vairaṇī; so we have heard. || 26 ||
Then the lord Kaśyapa accepted them as wives, as did Dharma, the venerable Soma, and likewise other great ṛṣis. || 27 ||
He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, twenty-seven to Soma, and four to Ariṣṭanemi. || 28 ||
Two indeed to Bahuputra, and likewise two to Aṅgiras;
two to the learned Kṛśāśva—listen to their names from me: || 29 ||
He who knows this entire creation of Dakṣa according to its true nature becomes long-lived, famous, prosperous, and possessed of offspring. || 29 ||
Arundhatī, Vasu, Yāmī, Lambā, Bhānu, Marutvatī, Saṃkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā, and likewise Viśvā. || 30 ||
These ten were his lawful wives; learn now of their offspring:
from Viśvā were born the Viśvedevas, and Sādhyā gave birth to the Sādhyas. || 31 ||
The sons of Marutvat were the Maruts; the sons of Vasu were the Vasus;
the sons of Bhānu were the Bhānus; and the sons of Muhūrta were the Muhūrtas. || 32 ||
From Lambā was born Ghoṣa, and from Yamī was born Nāgavīthī;
and from Arundhatī were born all the regions of the earth. || 33 ||
From Saṃkalpā, however, the universal soul was born as Saṃkalpa himself;
and from Nāgavīthī and Yāminī, the Vṛṣalas were born. || 34 ||
The other daughters whom Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, gave as wives to Soma—all of them are celebrated in the science of astronomy under the name of the lunar mansions (nakṣatras). || 34 ||
As for those other renowned gods who have light as their vanguard—the eight known as the Vasus—I shall describe them in detail. || 35 ||
Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa are remembered by name as the Vasus. (36)
Apasya’s sons were Vaitaṇḍya, Śrama, Śānta, and likewise Muni;
Dhruva’s son was the lord Kāla, the destroyer of the worlds.
The venerable Varcas was the son of Soma; by him one becomes radiant.
Dharas son was Draviṇa, as well as Hutahavyavaha. || 38 ||
Manohara, Śiśira, Prāṇa, and likewise Ramaṇa [are the sons of Anila].
Śivā is the wife of Anila; her son is Manojava. (39)
And the two sons of Anila were indeed Avijñātagati and [Vijñātagati].
As for Kumāra, the son of Agni, he was born from a clump of reeds. || 40 ||
Śākha, Viśākha, and Naigameya followed behind him;
he was known as Kārttikeya, the offspring of the Kṛttikās. || 41 ||
Skanda and Sanatkumāra were created from a portion of his splendor;
they know the son of Pratyūṣa to be the ṛṣi named Devala. || 42 ||
Devala also had two sons who were patient and wise;
Bṛhaspati’s sister, however, was an excellent woman who remained a celibate student.
Having attained perfection through yoga, she wandered through the entire world unattached;
she was indeed the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus. || 44 ||
In her was born the illustrious Viśvakarman, the lord of creatures, the creator of thousands of crafts, and the carpenter of the gods. || 45 ||
He was the maker of all ornaments and the best among artisans;
he indeed fashioned the celestial chariots for all the gods. || 46 ||
Men subsist upon the craft of that great-souled one;
Surabhi gave birth to the eleven Rudras from Kaśyapa.
Through the grace of Mahādeva and purified by asceticism, there arose Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Tvaṣṭṛ, and the heroic Rudra. || 48 ||
And the glorious son of Tvaṣṭṛ, Viśvarūpa of great fame;
and Hara, Bahurūpa, and Tryambaka, who are invincible.
Vṛṣākapi, Śambhu, Kapardin, Raivata, Mṛgavyādha, Śarva, and Kapālin, O best of the twice-born. (50)
These eleven Rudras have been described as the lords of the three worlds;
thus, the hundred Rudras of immeasurable splendor are fully enumerated.
O tigers among sages, hear now of the wives of Kaśyapa Prajāpati, by whom this world of moving and non-moving beings was pervaded. (51)
Aditi, Diti, Danu, Ariṣṭā, Surasā, Khaśā, Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhavaśā, and Irā. || 52 ||
O Brahmins, know that Kadrū and Muni were their offspring!
In the previous Manvantara, there were twelve excellent and supreme gods. (53)
They were called the Tuṣitas; they spoke to one another when the interval of Vaivasvata Manu had arrived, during the period of the highly illustrious Cākṣuṣa Manu: || 54 ||
For the benefit of all the worlds, having come together with one another, O gods, enter into Aditi quickly indeed. 55.
"Let us be born during a Manvantara; that will be for our welfare.
Having spoken thus, they all [did so] during the interval of Cākṣuṣa Manu. || 56 ||
Born from Kaśyapa Mārīca and Aditi, the daughter of Dakṣa, Viṣṇu and Śakra were indeed born there once again. || 57 ||
Aryaman, Dhātṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ, and likewise Pūṣan;
Vivasvat, Savitṛ, Mitra, and Varuṇa as well. || 58 ||
Aṃśa, Bhaga, and Atitejas—these are remembered as the twelve Ādityas who were formerly the Tuṣita gods during the Cākṣuṣa interval. || 59 ||
In the Vaivasvata interval, those twelve Ādityas are indeed recorded;
and those twenty-seven who are proclaimed as the wives of Soma, observers of great vows (mahāvrata). || 60 ||
From them were born offspring who were radiant and possessed immeasurable splendor;
there were sixteen children from the wives of Ariṣṭanemi.
Four types of *ṛc* verses are traditionally recorded for the learned Bahuputra: those born of Pratyāṅgirasa, which are excellent and honored by the Brahman-sages. || 62 ||
The divine weapons are said to belong to the celestial sage Kṛśāśva;
indeed, these are born once again at the end of a thousand yugas. || 63 ||
And here, O brahmins, the cessation and arising of all the hosts of gods belonging to the Thirty-three who are born of desire are also described. || 64 ||
Just as the rising and setting of the sun occur in the sky, so too do those hosts of gods come into being age after age. || 65 ||
We have heard that two sons were born to Diti from Kaśyapa:
Hiraṇyakaśipu and the powerful Hiraṇyākṣa. || 66 ||
And Siṃhikā became a daughter, the wife of Vipracitti;
her sons, who were of great strength, are known as the Saimhikeyas. || 67 ||
Hiraṇyakaśipu had four sons of renowned power: Anuhrāda, Hrāda, and the heroic Prahrāda. || 68 ||
And Saṃhrāda was the fourth; likewise, Hrāda was the son of Hrāda, and both Sunda and Nisunda were the sons of Saṃhrāda. The sons of Hrada were Āyuṣmat, Śibi, and Bāṣkala. || 69 ||
Virocana, the son of Prahrāda, was born, and from Virocana, Bali was born.
O you whose wealth is asceticism, Bali had a hundred sons, with Bāṇa as the eldest.
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Sūrya, Candramas, Indratāpana, Kumbhanābha, Gardabhākṣa, Kukṣi, and others such as these. || 71 ||
Among them, Bāṇa was the eldest and possessed of exceeding strength; he was dear to Paśupati.
In a former kalpa, having propitiated the Lord, the husband of Umā, Bāṇa requested these boons: "I shall sport by your side. || 71 ||
The five sons of Hiraṇyākṣa were wise and possessed of great strength:
Utkara, Śakuni, and likewise Bhūtasaṃtāpana.
Mahānābha, Vikrānta, and likewise Kālanābha—
there were also one hundred sons of Danu, possessed of fierce prowess.
I shall name those ascetics of great prowess according to their preeminence:
Dvimūrdhan, Śāṅkuni, and likewise the lord Śaṅkuśiras. (74)
Śāṅkukarṇa, Virādha, Gaveṣṭhī, and Dundubhi;
likewise Ayomukha, Śambara, Kapila, and Vāmana. || 75 ||
Mārīci, Maghavan, Irā, Gargaśiras, Vṛka, Vikṣobhaṇa, Ketu, Ketuvīrya, and Śatahrada; || 76 ||
Indrajit, Sarvajit, and likewise Vajranābha, Ekacakra, Mahābāhu, and Tāraka—all of great strength. || 77 ||
Vaiśvānara, Puloman, Vidrāvaṇa, Mahāśiras, Svarbhānu, Vṛṣaparvan, and Tuhuṇḍa were the great asuras. || 78 ||
Sūkṣma, Nicandra, Ūrṇanābha, Mahāgiri, Asiloman, Sukeśa, Śaṭha, Balaka, and Mada. || 79 ||
Likewise, Gaganamūrdhā, Kumbhanābha, Mahasura, Pramada, Maya, Kupatha, and the powerful Hayagrīva; || 80 ||
Vaiśravaṇa, Virūpākṣa, Supatha, Harāhara, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Śatamāya, and Śambara; || 81 ||
Śarabha, Śalabha, and the heroic Vipracitti—all these were sons of Danu, born from Kaśyapa. || 82 ||
Those Dānavas, headed by Vipracitti, were exceedingly powerful;
O best of the twice-born, it is impossible to enumerate their offspring, for their sons and grandsons are infinite in number due to their great multitude. || 82 ||
Prabhā was the daughter of Svarbhānu, and Śacī was the daughter of Puloman; Upadānavī, Hayaśirā, and Śarmiṣṭhā were the daughters of Vṛṣaparvan. || 83 ||
Pulomā and Kālikā, both daughters of Vaiśvānara, were the wives of Mārīci; they were both highly virtuous and possessed many offspring. || 84 ||
They had sixty thousand sons who were the delight of the Dānavas,
as well as another fourteen hundred who dwelt in Hiraṇyapura.
Endowed with great ascetic power, Mārīci begot the Paulomas and Kālakeyas, those Dānavas of immense strength. || 86 ||
For those inhabitants of Hiraṇyapura were indeed unslayable by the gods;
yet, by the grace of the Grandfather, they were slain by Savyasācin. || 87 ||
Pravāhaṇa was the son of Nahuṣa, and Jayanta was the son of Śacī. Then Śarmiṣṭhā gave birth to Puru, and Upadānavī bore Duṣmanta. || 88 ||
Then others, Dānavas of great heroism and extreme ferocity, were likewise born from Siṃhikā as the sons of Vipracitti. || 89 ||
Born from the union of Daityas and Dānavas, they were possessed of fierce prowess;
known as the Saiṃhikeyas, these thirteen were of great strength. || 90 ||
Vyaṃśa and Śalya were powerful, as was Nala of great strength;
likewise Vātāpi, Namuci, Ilvala, and Svasṛman. || 91 ||
Añjika and Naraka, as well as Kālanābha; Rāhu was indeed their eldest, the crusher of the sun and moon; and likewise Saramāna and the powerful Svarakalpa. || 92 ||
Mūka and Tuhuṇḍa were the two sons born of Hradā;
and Mārīca was born to Tāḍakā as the son of Sunda. || 93 ||
These were indeed the preeminent Dānavas who increased the lineage of Danu;
their sons and grandsons numbered in the hundreds and thousands. || 94 ||
In the lineage of the Daitya Saṃhrāda, the Nivātakavacas were born,
their souls purified by great ascetic penance.
Three crores of their sons resided in Maṇivatī;
they too were incapable of being slain even by the gods, yet they were struck down by Arjuna. || 96 ||
Six daughters of excellent character were proclaimed as the offspring of Tāmrā:
Kākī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Sugrīvī, Śuci, and Gṛdhrikā. || 97 ||
Kakī gave birth to crows, as well as owls and screech-owls; Śyenī produced hawks, Bhāsī produced bhāsas, and Gṛdhri produced vultures. || 98 ||
Śuci gave birth to flocks of aquatic birds, while Sugrīvī gave birth to horses, camels, and donkeys; these are proclaimed as the lineages of Tāmrā. || 99 ||
Vinatā had two sons, Aruṇa and Garuḍa;
Suparṇa was the best among birds, while they were fierce by virtue of their own karma. || 100 ||
There were also a thousand Surasās, serpents of immeasurable power, many-headed, high-souled beings who move through the sky. || 101 ||
But from Kadrū were born a thousand powerful Nāgas of immeasurable energy, who were subject to Suparṇa and possessed heads adorned with jewels. || 102 ||
Those whose principal [serpents] are always Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Airāvata, Mahāpadma, and both Kambala and Aśvatara. || 103 ||
Elāpatra, Padma, Karkoṭaka, Dhanamjaya, Mahānīla, Mahākarṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Balāhaka. || 104 ||
Kuhara, Puṣpadaṃṣṭra, Durmukha, and likewise Sumukha;
Śāṅkha, Śaṅkhapāla, Kapila, and Vāmana; Nahuṣa, Śāṅkharoman, Maṇi, and others such as these. || 105 ||
Their sons and grandsons— fourteen thousand cruel beings who feed on air— were struck down by Garuḍa.
Know that the *gaṇa* is Krodhavaśa; all fanged creatures—those born on land, birds, and those born from water—are recorded as the offspring of the Earth. || 106 ||
Surabhi gave birth to cows and likewise to buffaloes;
Irā produced trees, creepers, climbing plants, and all varieties of grasses.
Khaśā gave birth to the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, Muni to the Apsarases, and Ariṣṭā gave birth to the Gandharvas of great power. || 108 ||
These descendants of Kaśyapa, both stationary and moving, have been proclaimed;
their sons and grandsons numbered in the hundreds and thousands. || 109 ||
This creation of the sage is recorded as having occurred during the Svārociṣa Manvantara;
but now, during the great Vaivasvata Manvantara, at the extensive sacrifice of Varuṇa.
The creation of progeny by Brahmā while performing oblations is now described here;
therein [is told] how the seven mind-born Brahmarṣis were first produced.
The Grandfather himself ordained him as his son;
then, O twice-born one, there arose a conflict between the gods and the Dānavas. || 112 ||
Diti, whose sons had indeed been destroyed, propitiated Kaśyapa;
Kaśyapa, his soul being pleased by her having worshipped him perfectly, [spoke to her]. || 113 ||
He invited her to choose a boon, and she then chose this boon:
a son of immeasurable prowess, capable of slaying Indra. || 114 ||
And that great ascetic, being entreated, granted her a boon;
having bestowed the boon with a composed mind, Mārīca addressed her: || 115 ||
"Your son shall slay Indra within a hundred autumns, provided that you carry the fetus while remaining devoted to purity and established in your vow. || 116 ||
Having been addressed with "So be it" by that queen, the husband of great asceticism [accepted her word];
and she, pure and of excellent complexion, conceived a fetus.
Then he approached Diti; then,
having placed the embryo within Diti, Kaśyapa, firm in his vows,
delighted in that best of groups.
Of the gods of immeasurable splendor. || 118 ||
Having withdrawn his invincible splendor, which was incapable of being slain even by the immortals,
he went to the mountain itself.
Firm in his vows, he devoted himself to asceticism.
And Indra, the subduer of Pāka, became intent on finding a weakness in her;
when her hundred years were nearly complete, the infallible one perceived that vulnerability.
Without having performed the purification of her feet, Diti went to bed and fell asleep;
he entered her womb.
Then Vajrapāṇi cut that embryo into seven pieces;
as the embryo was being split apart by the vajra, it then cried out. || 121 ||
"Do not weep," Śakra said to him again and again;
yet that embryo became divided into seven parts, and Indra, enraged, [struck] it once more.
The subduer of enemies split each one of them into seven pieces with his thunderbolt;
they became the gods known as the Maruts, who were possessed of great strength. || 123 ||
Just as it was spoken by Maghavan, so indeed did the Maruts become;
and there were forty-nine gods who were the companions of the wielder of the thunderbolt. || 124 ||
O best of the twice-born, when those beings had thus multiplied,
he indeed took pleasure in that foremost of hosts.
Of the gods of immeasurable splendor. || 124 ||
O twice-born ones, Prajāpati Hari bestowed those kingdoms, beginning with that of Pṛthu, in succession upon each of the lineages. || 125 ||
He is Hari, the Supreme Person, the Hero, Kṛṣṇa, the Victorious One, and the Lord of Creatures; he is Parjanya, the Sun, and the Manifest—this entire world belongs to him. || 126 ||
O best of the twice-born, for one who correctly understands this creation of the elements and the auspicious birth of the Maruts, [there is liberation].
For one who hears and even reads [this], there is no fear of returning to this world; how then could there be fear of the next world? || 127 ||
To those very ones who had thus increased in power, Hari, the Lord of Creatures, duly bestowed this creation of beings.
Listen now to what has been told before you.
I. 22.1–13a) Thus, when all creatures had been created by the high-souled Kaśyapa, both the stationary and the moving were firmly established.
Having consecrated Pṛthu, the son of Vena, in the supreme sovereignty,
the Grandfather then proceeded to assign the various kingdoms in due order. || 1 ||
He consecrated Soma in the sovereignty over the twice-born, the plants, the constellations and the planets, as well as over sacrifices and ascetic penances.
He appointed Varuṇa to the sovereignty over the waters, Vaiśravaṇa as the lord of kings, and Bṛhaspati, the master of the Aṅgirases, over the Viśvedevas. || 3 ||
He consecrated Kavya, the lord of the Bhrigus, in the kingdom;
likewise, he consecrated Vishnu among the Adityas and Pavaka among the Vasus. || 4 ||
He appointed Dakṣa over the Prajāpatis, Vāsava over the Maruts,
and Prahlāda of immeasurable prowess over the Daityas and Dānavas. || 5 ||
He appointed Nārāyaṇa as the lord of the Sādhyas, the bull-bannered Śiva as the lord of the Rudras, and Vipracitti as the king of the Dānavas.
He consecrated Vaivasvata Yama in the sovereignty over the ancestors,
as well as over the yakṣas, the rākṣasas, and likewise the earthly kings.
Of all spirits and piśācas, he is the Lord of the Mountains (Śiva) who bears the trident;
of mountains, Himavat; and of rivers, the ocean. || 8 ||
Of scents, of the winds, of disembodied beings, and of those possessing sound and space—Vāyu is the most excellent among the powerful. (9)
He made Citraratha the lord and master of the oceans, the rivers, the clouds that send down rain, and the Gandharvas. || 10 ||
He made Vāsuki the chief of the nāgas, Takṣaka the chief of the serpents, and Śeṣa the chief of all fanged creatures.
He consecrated him as king. || 11 ||
Then he assigned Airāvata as the king of elephants,
and Uccaiḥśravas as the king of horses.
And Garuḍa among birds. || 12 ||
He consecrated Uccaiḥśravas as the king of horses,
and then [he consecrated] all the birds.
Garuḍa, the best among those who fly. || 12 ||
Then he consecrated the tiger as the king of wild beasts, the bull among cattle, and the Plakṣa tree as the king of the lords of the forest. || 13 ||
And likewise Kāmadeva, the lord of all the hosts of Apsarases and Gandharvas, as well as the seasons, the months, and the days; (14)
Of the fortnights and nights, of the lunar phases and their opposites,
of the moments, lunar days, and festivals; of the moments and the festivals,
of the measures of the *kalās* and *kāṣṭhās*, and likewise of the seasons and the two solstices.
Then, for the sake of calculation and yoga, he made Saṃvatsara the lord of the cycle.
Having thus divided the kingdoms in due order, the Grandfather then [appointed] the guardians of the quarters.
He established [it] everywhere. || 15 ||
In the eastern direction, [he appointed] Sudhanvan, the son of Vairāja Prajāpati,
as the guardian of the quarter.
He consecrated him as king. || 16 ||
In the southern direction, he consecrated as king the son of Kardama Prājāpati, named Śaṅkhapada. || 17 ||
In the western direction, he consecrated the high-souled King Ketumān, the son of Rajas, as the imperishable sovereign. || 18 ||
Likewise, he consecrated Hiraṇyaroman as the invincible king over the northern quarter of Parjanya, the son of Prajāpati. || 19 ||

He made Vaivasvata Manu the sovereign of human beings. This entire earth, with its seven continents and its cities, is even today governed by him according to his domain through righteousness. || 20 ||
In the previous Svāyambhuva interval, they were consecrated by Brahmā;
for these kings who become Manus are indeed consecrated [in this manner]. (20)

For when the past Manvantaras have passed away, the kings who lived during those periods have likewise gone; thus others are consecrated when a new Manvantara arrives. All those who have passed and those yet to come are recorded as the lords of the Manvantaras. || 202 ||
But Pṛthu, the lord of men, having been consecrated by these kings in the sovereignty of kings according to the ritual prescribed in the Vedas, was anointed with the Rājasūya sacrifice. || 21 ||
Then, when the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara of immeasurable splendor had passed, he assigned sovereignty over the earth to Vaivasvata Manu. || 211 ||
I shall relate in detail the history of Vaivasvata Manu for your benefit, if you desire to hear it here;
for this is a great foundation established in the Purāṇa. || 212 ||
[It is auspicious, bringing wealth, fame, long life, and residence in heaven.
Section 2: Genealogy | Chapter 4 (Aligned with Bd. I. 36.117–37.22a; Br. 4.19–122; H. 283–405; Śidh. 56.1–57.26; Vā.
62.99–63.21) The Sages said:
O high-minded one, relate in detail the birth of Pṛthu,
and how in former times the earth was milked by that great-souled one.
And just as it was milked by the ancestors, by the gods, by the great seers,
and by the Daityas and Nāgas;
Just as by the yakṣas, just as by the trees. || 2 ||
Just as by the mountains, by the piśācas, by the gandharvas, by the best of the twice-born,
and by the rākṣasas of great being,
Just as the earth was milked. || 3 ||
O observer of noble vows, you should also tell us about their specific vessels and the specific varieties of milk for their calves.
And [he described] the milkers in due order. || 4 ||
And for what reason was Vena’s hand churned in former times by the ancient great seers who were filled with wrath? Proclaim that cause as well.
Sūta (Lomaharṣaṇa) said:
O best of the twice-born, I shall proclaim to you the origin of Pṛthu, the son of Vena; listen with one-pointed attention and self-restraint.

O Brahmins, I would not proclaim this, nor describe this Brahman, to one who is impure, to one of base mind, to one who is sinful, nor to one who is not a disciple, nor to one who lacks vows, nor to one who is not a disciple and is harmful.
Nor to one who is ungrateful or harmful; nor under any circumstances to one who does not observe vows.
Listen truly to this secret proclaimed by the sages, which leads to heaven, brings fame, bestows long life, confers prosperity, and is in perfect accord with the Vedas! || 8 ||
Whoever, having paid homage to the Brahmins, should constantly recount this account of the origin of Pṛthu, the son of Vena, shall not grieve over what has been done or left undone. || 9 ||
He was indeed the protector of dharma; that lord, the protector of dharma, was formerly equal to Atri. Born from the lineage of Atri, he was the Prajāpati named Aṅga. || 10 ||
His son was Vena, who was not particularly righteous;
he was born as a lord of creatures (prajāpati) to Sunīthā, the daughter of Mṛtyu. || 11 ||
Due to the fault of his maternal grandfather, Vena, the grandson of Kāla,
cast his own duty behind him and, driven by desire, indulged in greed.
That king established a law devoid of righteousness;
transgressing the Vedic duties, he became devoted to unrighteousness. || 13 ||
"I shall tell you, O Brahmins; listen, I shall proclaim it. Alas!
While he ruled, his subjects were deprived of Vedic study and the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ* call. The deities did not partake of the Soma offered in the sacrifices. || 14 ||
"No sacrifice is to be performed, no oblation is to be offered"—this was the cruel vow of that Prajāpati when destruction was imminent. || 15 ||
I am to be sacrificed to and worshipped by gods and men in sacrifice;
sacrifices are to be ordained unto me, and offerings are likewise to be poured into me. || 16 ||
Then all the great seers, headed by Marīci, spoke to him as he was transgressing the bounds of propriety and acting most improperly: || 17 ||
"We shall enter upon initiation for many groups of years;
do not practice unrighteousness, O Vena, for this is the eternal dharma. || 18 ||
Born from Atri at the conclusion [of the sacrifice], you are undoubtedly a Prajāpati;
"And I shall protect the subjects"—this was the covenant you made. || 19 ||
To all those great seers who were speaking thus, the evil-minded Vena, ignorant of what was beneficial, then laughed and said this: || 20 ||
Who else is the creator of dharma, or whom should I listen to? Or who on earth is equal to me in learning, heroism, austerity, and truth? (21)
Surely you, being deluded and lacking discernment, do not know me— the source of all beings and especially of all phenomena. || 22 ||
If I so desired, I could burn the earth, or likewise flood it with waters;
I could even obstruct both heaven and earth—
of this there is no need for deliberation.
When King Vena could not be persuaded because of his delusion and arrogance, the great seers then became enraged. || 24 ||
Having restrained that trembling one of great strength, those high-souled ones, filled with wrath,
then churned his left thigh. || 25 ||
While that [ocean] was being churned, indeed, a man was born from the thigh of the king;
he was exceedingly tall and also dark-complexioned. || 26 ||
Terrified, with his senses agitated, he stood with palms joined in reverence.
Seeing him thus distraught, Atri then said to him, "Sit down. || 27 ||
He, of infinite prowess, became the founder of the Niṣāda lineage;
he also produced the fishermen, who were born from the impurity of Vena.
And those others who dwell in the Vindhya mountains—the Tukhāras and the Tumburus, as well as those who delight in unrighteousness—know them to be defiled by the stain of Vena. || 29 ||
Then once again those great-souled ones, their anger aroused, vigorously churned the right hand of Vena like a fire-drill. || 30 ||
From him was born Pṛthu, who resembled a blazing fire;
because he was born from the palm of Pṛthu’s hand, he is therefore called Pṛthu.
Shining with his own body, he blazed like Agni himself. (31)
That highly illustrious Pr̥thu was born already equipped with a bow and armor;
he took up the primordial, great-sounding bow named Ājagava, as well as divine arrows and a brilliantly radiant coat of mail for his protection. || 32 ||
When he was born, all living beings were filled with joy;
they gathered around the great king, and Vena ascended to the third heaven. || 33 ||
Then that tiger among men, the royal sage, was rescued from the hell named Put, by his high-souled and virtuous son who had been born. || 34 ||
Then the oceans and the rivers, bringing all kinds of jewels and waters for the purpose of the consecration, all approached him. || 35 ||
And the blessed Grandfather, together with the gods and the descendants of Aṅgiras, as well as all beings, both stationary and moving, [were present]. 36.
Having assembled, they then consecrated Vainya as the lord of men, the protector of subjects, endowed with great splendor, with the grand sovereignty of a king. || 37 ||

Thus consecrated according to the prescribed rites by the gods, the sons of Aṅgiras, who were experts in dharma, that highly resplendent Pṛthu, the son of Vena, became the majestic sovereign king over all monarchs. || 38 ||
His subjects were first won over by his father and then won over by him;
because of that affection for him, the name "Rāja" (King) arose for him—hence the name Rāja was born from his affection. (39) It was born from affection. (39)
The waters solidified for him as he advanced toward the ocean;
the mountains yielded the way, and there was no snapping of his banner. || 40 ||
The earth yields crops without being ploughed; foods are prepared by mere thought;
cows grant all desires; and in every leaf-cup there is honey. || 41 ||
At that very time, during the auspicious sacrifice of the Grandfather (Brahmā), the high-minded Sūta was born from the *sūti* at the conclusion of the pressing day (*sautya-hani*). || 42 ||

At that very great sacrifice, the wise Māgadha was born. While the Sāman-singers were chanting over the sacrificial vessels used for the Vaiśvadeva rite, he was produced during that Sāman-song; therefore, he is called a Māgadha. || 42 ||
With the oblation belonging to Indra, he offered as an oblation mixed with that of Bṛhaspati to the god Indra; from that, a charioteer (sūta) was born. || 42 ||
In that regard, negligence arose concerning the ritual acts and the expiation,
because the teacher’s oblation was defiled and overwhelmed by the sacrificial offering of the disciple.
Through the reversal of high and low status, that corruption of caste arose;
and that which was born as Brahminhood from the Kṣatriya, originating from a lower womb. || 42 ||
The Sūta is proclaimed to have similar duties due to his similarity with the former;
for this is the middle status of the Sūta, whose duty is to subsist by the profession of a Kṣatriya. || 42 ||
The movements of chariots, elephants, and horses, as well as the lowest form of medical treatment—for the purpose of praising Pṛthu—those two were summoned there by the great seers. || 43 ||
Then all the ṛṣis said: "Let this king be praised; this deed is worthy of you both, and this lord of men is a fitting recipient. || 44 ||
Then those two, the Sūta and the Māgadha, said to all those ṛṣis:
"We please both the gods and the ṛṣis by means of our own duties. (45)
"O twice-born ones, we do not know her deeds, nor her fame characterized by such qualities, by which we might compose a hymn of praise for this radiant queen. || 46 ||
The ṛṣis then enjoined them both, saying: "Let him be praised for his future deeds—he who is constantly devoted to the dharma of giving, truthful in speech, and has his senses fully controlled. (461)
Jñānaśila was generous and remained undefeated in battles;
he performed those deeds which Pṛthu, possessed of great strength, performed later. || 47 ||
This lord of men is truthful in speech, generous by nature, true to his promises,
illustrious, victorious, patient, valiant, and one whose commands are seen to be obeyed.

A king who knows the Dharma, who is grateful, compassionate, and pleasant of speech; who honors those worthy of honor, performs sacrifices, is devoted to Brahman, and is true to his word; who is self-controlled, tranquil, diligent, and established in the administration of justice. || 472 ||
From that time forth, O best of sages, blessings have indeed been employed in hymns of praise throughout the world.
[He was honored] by bards, panegyrists, and heralds. || 48 ||
At the conclusion of their praise, Pṛthu, the lord of subjects, being well-pleased, bestowed the Anūpa region upon Sūta and the Magadha region upon Māgadha. || 49 ||
Seeing him, the subjects were exceedingly joyful, and the great seers said:
"This lord of men will be the provider of livelihoods for you. (50)
Then, at the word of the great seers, "Provide for us a means of livelihood," the subjects flocked together toward the highly fortunate Vainya. || 51 ||
Thus pursued by his subjects, yet desiring to act for their welfare,
the powerful one took up his bow and arrows and struck the earth.
Then, terrified by the fear of Vainya, the Earth fled away, having become a cow;
Pṛthu, taking up his bow, pursued her as she ran. || 53 ||
Having traveled through the worlds beginning with the world of Brahmā out of fear of Vainya,
she then beheld Vainya before her, holding his bow.
With blazing, sharpened arrows, he struck Acyuta, who was radiant with splendor, the great yogin, the high-souled one, who is unassailable even by the immortals. || 55 ||
Finding no protection, she approached Vainya alone, joining her palms in reverence, she who is always worthy of worship by the three worlds. (56)
He said to the son of Vena: "Do you not perceive the unrighteousness in the killing of a woman?
O King, how will you sustain the subjects without me? (57)
The worlds are established in me, O King; by me this universe is sustained. Know this, O ruler of the earth: without me, all creatures would perish. || 58 ||
"You ought not to kill me, O protector of the earth, if you desire to act for the welfare of all creatures; listen to these words of mine! (59)
All undertakings commenced with skillful means succeed;
consider a means, O King, by which you may sustain your subjects. || 60 ||
"O King, even having slain me, you will not be capable of protecting your subjects;
I shall simply have been experienced [by you]. Restrain your anger, O one of great splendor! (61)
O protector of the earth, they say that women are not to be slain even among beings born as animals; you ought not to abandon righteousness. || 62 ||
Having heard these various words, the high-minded and righteous king restrained his anger and spoke thus to the earth: || 63 ||

Whoever, for the sake of a single purpose, should kill many living beings or even just one—whether for oneself or for another; or whoever kills even a single life or many lives—there shall be a transgression for him in this world; his action is a transgression. || 64 ||
Many prosper in happiness when that which is auspicious has been slain, and when that which is inauspicious has been slain;
when that [evil] is killed, there is no merit nor even a minor offense. || 65 ||
"When the death of one evildoer brings security to many, that killing bestows merit.
Therefore, O Earth, for the sake of my subjects, I shall slay you.
If you do not carry out my word today for the benefit of the world. || 66 ||
Having slain you today with an arrow for turning away from my command, I shall manifest myself and personally sustain the subjects. || 67 ||

Therefore, abiding by my command, O best among the upholders of Dharma, restore all living beings to life; restore all creatures to life forever, for you are indeed capable of sustaining them. You are certainly able, without a doubt.
And become my daughter; then I shall restrain this arrow of terrible aspect as it rises up for the purpose of slaying you. || 69 ||
Having been addressed in this manner, the Earth then replied to the son of Vena:
"O hero, I shall perform all of this; of this there is no doubt. (70)
"All undertakings undertaken with skillful means succeed;
find a means by which you may sustain these subjects.
But look upon that calf of mine, so that I, out of maternal affection, may continue to yield my milk."
And make me level everywhere, O best among the upholders of dharma. || 71 ||
"Just as my flowing milk shall permeate everything,
so he then cleared away hundreds of thousands of mountains."
Then, by means of the tip of his bow, the son of Vena caused the mountains to be leveled;
thus King Pṛthu, the son of Vena, made the earth even.
Throughout the past Manvantaras, the Earth had been uneven. (73)
By its very nature, it consists of both even and uneven surfaces;
indeed, this is said to have existed thus in the past during the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara.
Indeed, during that previous creation, on this uneven surface of the earth, there was at that time no division of cities or villages. || 75 ||
There were no crops, no cattle-rearing, no agriculture, and no trade routes;
there was neither truth nor falsehood, neither greed nor envy.
In this Vaivasvata interval, which has now arrived, the origin of all this in this world began from the time of Vainya. || 77 ||
O twice-born ones, wherever that ground was level at that time,
there all the subjects [settled].
They chose their dwelling place. || 78 ||
The food for the people consisted of fruits and roots;
thus, they were joined with great hardship, and so it was reported to Anuśūra. || 79 ||
Having fashioned Manu Svāyambhuva as his calf,
that tiger among men [placed him] upon his own hand.
From that, he milked the earth. || 80 ||
The powerful Pṛthu, son of Vena, [caused] all species of grain to grow;
by that food, all the subjects [were sustained].
They continue to exist even today, possessing all knowledge. || 81 ||
It is also heard that the earth was milked again by the sages;
Soma became their calf, and Bṛhaspati was the milker. || 82 ||
The Vedic meters, beginning with the Gāyatrī, were their vessel;
at that time, their austerity and the eternal Brahman were their milk. || 83 ||
Furthermore, it is heard that after that, the hosts of gods, led by Puraṃdara, took a golden vessel and milked this earth. || 84 ||
Vatsa was Maghavan, and the Lord Savitṛ was the milker; the milk was indeed strengthening, by which the deities subsist. || 85 ||
It is also heard that the Earth was milked again by the ancestors of immeasurable prowess, who took up a silver vessel and [offered] the *svadhā* oblation. (86)
The nectar of the *svadhā* offering belonged to the ancestors; likewise, Aryaman was the milker. Yama Vaivasvata was their calf, the majestic one;
and Antaka, Time, the destroyer of the worlds, became the milker. (87)
And it is heard that the Earth was then milked by the Nāgas, having made Takṣaka the calf;
taking a gourd as their vessel, they drew forth poison as the milk. || 88 ||
O best of the twice-born, this applies indeed to all the Nāgas and the Sarpas in every respect. || 89 ||
It is also heard that the Earth was milked again by the Asuras,
who took an iron vessel and [milked] the illusory power that destroys enemies. || 91 ||
At that time, Virocana, the son of Prahlāda, was their calf;
the mighty Dvimūrdhan was the officiating priest of the Daityas, and Madhu was the milker. || 92 ||
By means of that very illusion, even today all these illusory asuras continue to exist,
possessing immeasurable wisdom.
Therefore, their strength is immeasurable. || 93 ||
O King, it is heard that the Earth was milked again by the Yakṣas; this Earth was milked once more into an unbaked clay vessel, and she became invisible. 94.
With that milk, the yakṣas,
the rākṣasas who resemble immortals,
and the piśācas sustain themselves.
And likewise the hosts of spirits. || 99 ||
Furthermore, that [cow] was milked by the Gandharvas together with the hosts of Apsarases into a lotus-leaf vessel, having made Citraratha the calf and likewise using pure fragrances. || 100 ||
Among them, Vasuruci was the son of the sage Śuci; he was the milk-cow’s milker, a Gandharva king of great soul and exceeding strength, resplendent like the sun. || 101 ||
And it is heard that the goddess Earth was milked again by the mountains;
there, the medicinal herbs in embodied form and various kinds of jewels [were obtained]. || 102 ||
Vatsa was Himavat, the great mountain Meru was the milker, and the vessel was indeed Śaila; by him the mountains were established. || 103 ||
It is heard that the Earth was milked again by the trees and creepers, who took a vessel made of Palāśa wood for the purpose of regenerating what had been cut down or burnt. || 104 ||

The flowering *śāla* tree is the wish-fulfiller; the *plakṣa* tree is the calf for those who possess glory. She who milks all desires is the cow who yields every wish; she is the producer of all crops, the Earth, the sustainer of all beings. || 105 ||

This Earth—the nourisher, the ordainer, the purifier, and the sustainer of wealth—was indeed milked by Pṛthu for the benefit of the worlds; so we have heard. She is the foundation and the very source of all that is moving and unmoving. (106)
This earth was renowned as "Medinī" because it extended to the ends of the ocean;
and because it supports wealth (*vasu*), it is called "Vasudhā.
Furthermore, it was entirely drenched with the fat (*medas*) of Madhu and Kaiṭabha. || 107 ||
Therefore, this goddess Earth is called *Medinī* by those who discourse upon Brahman;
this was due to her acceptance by the wise King Pṛthu, the son of Vena.
The goddess attained the status of a daughter and is called Pṛthvī;
she was divided and purified by Pṛthu as the bearer of wealth.
It was prosperous, abounding in grain and mines, and adorned with a garland of cities and towns. || 110 ||
Such was the power of that king Vainya, the best of monarchs;
he was undoubtedly worthy of homage and worship by all the hosts of living beings. || 111 ||
And by the highly fortunate Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, Pṛthu alone—being the eternal source of the Brahman—is to be saluted. || 112 ||
And by illustrious kings desiring the status of sovereignty, the majestic Pṛthu, son of Vena, the first king, is to be saluted. || 113 ||
Even by warriors who are valiant and desirous of victory in battle, he is the original initiator of wars; indeed, he is the first king among warriors, and thus Pṛthu alone is worthy of homage. 114.
For whatever warrior goes to battle after proclaiming King Pṛthu, he, being renowned, crosses through even the most terrible conflicts in safety. || 115 ||
Even by wealthy Vaiśyas who follow the prescribed conduct of a Vaiśya, Pṛthu alone—the highly illustrious bestower of livelihoods—is to be honored with salutation. || 116 ||
In the same way, Śūdras who are pure and serve the three higher castes must likewise pay homage to Pṛthu alone if they desire the highest welfare. || 116 ||
These specific calves, the milkers, the milk itself, and the vessels have been described by me;
what more shall I describe to you? || 117 ||
## Section 3: The Manvantaras (Book III. 1.3–116; Br. 5.1–64; H. 406–544; Śidh. 58.2b–82; Vā. 100.3–118; cf. Mr.
94) The Sages said:
O Great-minded One, [please describe] all the Manvantaras in detail.
O Lomaharṣaṇa, proclaim their former creation as well! || 1 ||
O Sūta, we wish to hear in accordance with reality how many Manus there have been, for how long a time they lasted, and what the Manvantaras were. || 2 ||
Sūta (Lomaharṣaṇa) said:
O Brahmins, it is not possible to describe the details of all the Manvantaras even in hundreds of years; therefore, O twice-born ones, listen to them in brief! || 3 ||
First was Svāyambhuva Manu, then Manu Svārociṣa;
likewise Auttama, Tāmasa, Raivata, and Cākṣuṣa.
And Vaivasvata, O Brahmins, is currently called Manu; likewise Sāvarṇi, Bhautya, and Raucya are Manus as well. (5)
In the same way, four Manus named Merusāvarṇa are recorded—those who have passed, those who are present, and likewise those who are yet to come. || 6 ||
These Manus have been recounted to you by me exactly as they were heard;
now I shall declare their sages, as well as their sons and the hosts of gods.
Marīci, the venerable Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, and Vasiṣṭha—these seven are the sons of Brahmā. || 8 ||
Likewise, O twice-born ones, in the northern direction were the Seven Sages, and during the Svāyambhuva interval there were the gods known as the Yāmas. || 9 ||
Āgnīdhra, Agnibāhu, Medhā, Medhātithi, Vasu, Jyotiṣmān, Dyutimān, Havya, and Savana were his sons. || 10 ||
These ten sons of great power were the sons of Svāyambhuva Manu;
this, O Brahmins, is declared to be the first Manvantara. || 11 ||
Aurva, the son of Vasiṣṭha, Stamba, and Kāśyapa;
Prāṇa and Bṛhaspati; likewise Bhārgava, Prāṇa, Datta, and Niścyavana; and Ṛṣabha, the son of Aṅgiras. || 12 ||
And Paulastya, as well as Dattātri;
likewise Ātreya and Niścala; then Paulaha and Arvarīvan.
And these are the seven ṛṣis. || 12 ||
These great seers of mighty vows, proclaimed by Vāyu, were there;
and the gods known as the Tuṣitas are remembered as having existed during the Svārociṣa interval. || 13 ||
Havirdhra, Sukṛti, Jyotis, Āpas, Mūrti, Ayasmaya, Prathīta, Nabhasya, Nabha, and likewise Ūrja. || 14 ||
O brahmins, those sons of the high-souled Manu Svārociṣa have been proclaimed as protectors of the earth, possessed of great heroism and prowess. || 15 ||
This second Manvantara has been described by me, O Brahmins.
I shall now speak of this third one; understand it, O best of the twice-born!
There were seven sons of Vasiṣṭha, renowned as the Vāsiṣṭhas.
The sons of Hiraṇyagarbha were named Ūrja, who were possessed of great splendor. || 17 ||
The sages have been mentioned here by me; listen as they are being proclaimed—the ten beautiful sons of Uttama, O best of munis. || 18 ||
Iṣa, Ūrja, Tanūja, Madhu, and Mādhava;
Śuci, Śukra, Sahas, Nabhasya, and Nabha. || 19 ||
The Bhānava gods are present there; thus the Manvantara has been described. Now, however, I shall speak of the fourth Manvantara. || 20 ||
O best of the twice-born, Kāvya, Pṛthu, Agni, Janyu, Dhātṛ, Kapīvān, and Akapīvān were the seven Ṛṣis there, O brahmins. || 21 ||
O twice-born ones, the sons and grandsons of Manu, as well as the hosts of gods, who were virtuous, have been proclaimed in the Purāṇa as belonging to the Tāmasa Manvantara. || 22 ||
[And I shall now declare the sons of Tāmasa Manu, O King:
Dyuti, Tapasya, Sutapas, Tapomūla, Tapośana, Taporati, Akalmāṣa, Tanvī, Dhanvī, and Paraṃtapa. || 23 ||
O best of sages, these ten sons of great strength were born of the Tāmasa Manu, as proclaimed by Vāyu; this is the fourth intermediate period (antara). || 24 ||
Vedabāhu, Yadudhra, and the sage Vedaśiras; likewise Hiraṇyaroman, Parjanya, Ūrdhvabāhu, and Somapa. || 25 ||
Satyanetra, as well as these other seven ṛṣis; and the gods known as Abhūtarajas, as well as others who are Prakṛtis. (26)
Pāriplava and Raibhya are said to be the interval between the Manus;
now, learn from me as I speak of his sons: || 27 ||
He is steadfast, imperishable, disciplined, a seer of reality, free from longing, forest-dwelling, luminous, devoid of delusion, truthful, and accomplished. || 28 ||
The sons of Raivata were the [kings]; this is the fifth interval.
Now I shall fully declare the sixth; understand it, O best of the twice-born! || 29 ||
Bhṛgu, Nabha, Vivasvat, Sudhāman, Virajas, Atināman, and Sahiṣṇu—these seven are indeed the great seers (maharṣis). || 30 ||
O brahmins, during the interval of Cākṣuṣa Manu, these gods are recorded as having been the Ādyas, Prabhūtas, Ṛbhavas, and Pṛthukas among the dwellers of heaven.
And the five classes of gods, O Brahmins, are known by name as the Lekhas;
they are the sons of the great-souled and highly energetic seer Aṅgiras.
O best of sages, during the interval of Cākṣuṣa Manu, there were ten famous sons of Nāḍvaleyā, beginning with Ūru, who were all wise brahmins.
The sixth Manvantara has been declared; now learn of the seventh:
Atri, Vasiṣṭha, and the venerable Kaśyapa, the great Ṛṣi.
Then Gautama, Bharadvāja, and likewise Viśvāmitra,
as well as the high-souled and venerable son of Ṛcīka.
And the seventh is Jamadagni; these are the sages currently in heaven.
Likewise, the Sādhyas, Rudras, Viśvedevas, Vasus, and Maruts [are there]. (36)
The Ādityas and the two Aśvins are remembered as the deities belonging to Vaivasvata;
they exist during this present interval of Manu Vaivasvata. || 37 ||
And the ten sons of that great-souled one, headed by Ikṣvāku—of these aforementioned great seers of immense power. || 38 ||
O twice-born ones, their sons and grandsons were seven groups of seven in all directions throughout all the Manvantaras of the past.
They remain for the purpose of establishing the Dharma and for the protection of the world;
when a Manvantara has passed, these groups consist of four times seven.
Having performed their duty, they go to heaven, to the stainless world of Brahmā. Others, endowed with austerity, likewise fill that station;
both those of the past and those of the present, O twice-born ones, do so by this sequence. || 41 ||
The sages said:
All the previous Manvantaras, along with those that follow,
as well as the present interval of this current Manu, belong to these very same Seven Sages.
Tell us everything, in full detail and in proper sequence, regarding the extensive nature and the constituent parts of that great-souled one’s natural disposition. || 41 ||
Sūta said:
O best of sages, I shall relate all of this to you exactly as it is, including this fourth quarter along with its dissolution.
O twice-born ones, listen to this creation of the high-souled Manu Vaivasvata, the present one, in detail and in its proper sequence.
Listen as I speak in brief of the seven future Manvantaras, along with the dissolution of the worlds! (41)
These seven Manvantaras have indeed been correctly described by me in brief; now hear from me about those that are yet to come! || 42 ||
There will be five future Manus of the Sāvarṇa lineage; learn of them:
one of them is Vaivasvata, while four belong to Prajāpati.
O Brahmin, these sons of Parameṣṭhin became the Merusāvarṇas;
for they were the grandsons of Dakṣa and the sons of Priyā, who became kings. || 44 ||
Endowed with great ascetic power and possessing immense luster, they dwelt upon the summit of Mount Meru.
The son of the Prajāpati Ruci, known as Raucya, is remembered as a Manu;
and the son of Ruci born of the goddess Bhūti is named Bhautya. || 45 ||
I shall now proclaim, in brief, the future history of the future Manu Sāvarṇa, the son of Vivasvat; listen to that! || 45 ||
And these seven great sages who are to come in the future, O twice-born ones, are remembered as having attained their positions in heaven during the interval of Manu Sāvarṇa here on earth.
Rāma, Vyāsa, as well as Atri,
renowned as the Radiant One (Dīptimān), Kauśika, and Gālava.
And [there was] Jāmadagnya Bhārgava. || 46 ||
Dvaipāyana, Vasiṣṭha,
Kṛpa Śāradvata, and likewise the radiant Atri.
Ṛṣyaśṛṅga was the son of Kaśyapa;
likewise, the son of Bharadvāja was Aśvatthāman, the son of Droṇa, who possessed great splendor.
And Gautama’s own son was Gautama named Śaradvān,
as well as Gālava of the Kauśika lineage.
And Ruru Kāśyapa as well—these seven high-souled ones shall be the future best of sages. || 48 ||
These seven seers are remembered as being equal to Brahmā,
blessed by both their noble birth and their asceticism.
Likewise, by means of the explanations of the mantras. || 481 ||
The stainless Brahman-sages are remembered as being established in the Brahma-world;
they possess knowledge of the past, the future, and the present.
And those who have awakened by themselves; || 482 ||
But those who are renowned for their asceticism, who are disciplined and contemplative,
and [versed] in mantra, grammar, and so forth—
And those who [possess] sovereignty in every respect; || 483 ||
Having understood these, along with their names as "naiṣṭhika" (final), together with his wife—
these seven [are established] by means of the seven.
By virtue of their qualities, they are remembered as the Seven Sages (Saptarṣis). || 484 ||
Long-lived, creators of mantras,
lords, and far-sighted,
they perceive the Dharma directly through their own intelligence.
Likewise, they are the initiators of the spiritual lineage. || 485 ||
In all the ages known as Kṛta and the rest, again and again,
there were those of great austerity and those of immeasurable luster.
And there are three principal groups;
each of those groups of gods is traditionally said to consist of twenty members. || 481 ||
I shall now declare their names; listen with concentrated minds:
Rtu, Tapa, and Śukra.
Splendor, light, and the maker of radiance. || 482 ||
Prabhāsa, Bhāsakṛt, Dharma, Tejas, Raśmi, Kratu, Virāj, Arciṣmān, Dyotana, and Bhānu.
Yaśas, Kīrti, Budha, and Dhṛti—
these twenty are indeed proclaimed by their names as the Sutapas. || 483 ||
The Lord, the All-pervading, the Radiant, the Conqueror, the Destroyer, the Worthy One, the Season,
the One of Excellent Intellect, the One of Great Intellect, and the Resplendent.
The great one is called "Mahas," meaning the Great. || 484 ||
Deha, Muni, Naya, Jyeṣṭha, Samas, Satyas, and Viśrutas—
these indeed are the immeasurable ones.
Twenty have been proclaimed. || 485 ||
They cause the social classes and the stages of life to proceed in every respect.
The highly fortunate Seven Sages are devoted to truth and righteousness; and from their lineage were born [the following].
Births occur again and again. || 487 ||
Likewise, when the Dharma had become lax, the authors of the Mantras and Brāhmaṇas were the seven givers of boons.
Requested from others alone, || 488 ||
Therefore, neither time nor age is a criterion for the state of being a seer (*ṛṣi*).
This is the designation of the Seven Seers (*saptarṣika*).
It has been explained to you by me, O King. || 489 ||
They were indeed the sons of Mārīca, the high-souled Kaśyapa.
They will belong to Sāvarṇa, the Manu of the present; their Indra will be Bali, the son of Virocana, as he was in former times. || 491 ||
Vīravān, Avarīyas, Sumanta, Dhṛtimān, Vasu,
Cariṣṇu, Ārya, Dhṛṣṇu, Vāja, and Sumati— these will be the sons of Sāvarṇi Manu, the best of sages. || 50 ||
I shall now describe nine others among the future Sāvarṇi Manvantaras;
there will be other Sāvarṇi Manus, the sons of Brahmā.
These four, whom Meru described, were indeed possessed of divine vision;
for they were the grandsons of Dakṣa, the sons of his daughter Kriyā. || 502 ||
Endowed with great ascetic power and possessed of mighty energy, they were born upon the summit of Mount Meru by Brahmā and others, as well as by the wise Dakṣa himself.
Having gone to Maharloka, they will return and take refuge on Mount Meru;
those of great majesty were born previously in the Cākṣuṣa interval.
The sages said: How were the sons begotten by Dakṣa upon his own daughter, and [how were they begotten] by Bhava, by Brahmā, and by the high-souled Dharma? || 505 ||
Sūta said:
Therefore, having offered salutations to Pracetas, I shall describe those who will be the Sāvarṇa Manus, as well as their birth and their power. || 506 ||
For when the Vaivasvata [Manvantara] had been touched upon and the Cākṣuṣa was slightly remaining,
those Manus were indeed born for the future and upcoming interval.
The sons of Manu who were the grandsons of Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, are five by name; four of them were born of the supreme ṛṣis. || 508 ||
But Sāvarṇa, the son of Saṃjñā, was one;
likewise, the eldest son of Saṃjñā is named Manu Vaivasvata, the lord. || 509 ||
When the Vaivasvata interval arrived, the auspicious birth of those two took place.
These fourteen Manus have been proclaimed, who increase one's fame. || 5010 ||
In the Vedas, the Smṛtis, and the Purāṇas, all of them are described as sovereign lords;
they are all established as the lords of progeny and the lords of all beings. || 5011 ||
By them, this entire earth— with its seven continents and its cities—
is indeed to be protected by those lords of men for a full thousand yugas.
Through their progeny and through austerity, the detailed account of them will be told.
These emanations, beginning with Svāyaṃbhuva, are to be known as exactly fourteen. || 5013 ||
At the beginning of each Manvantara and other such periods, they appear here one by one;
having relinquished their offices, they take refuge in Maharloka.
Of those who have passed away, eight and likewise six others were among the former ones; and now this lord Vaivasvata is the sixtieth. || 5015 ||
I shall proclaim those who remain, together with the celestial rishis and the dānavas, along with all the future twice-born ones and the creation of progeny. || 5016 ||
The detailed account of them should be understood through the creation of Vivasvat;
for they are all from Vivasvat, neither deficient nor redundant. || 5017 ||
However, because of the great abundance of repetitions, I shall not provide a detailed account of them in the auspicious future Manvantaras, nor likewise in those that have already passed. || 5018 ||
Therefore, the innate dispositions in each family should be understood according to their respective divisions;
indeed, for the sake of their accomplishment, they are explained in detail and in due order. || 5019 ||
The daughter of Dakṣa was the most righteous, renowned by the name Suvratā;
she was the eldest, the best among all maidens, and the daughter of Viriṇī. || 5020 ||
Having taken that maiden, her father went into the presence of Brahmā, who was seated upon the Vairāja throne, together with Dharma and Bhava. || 5021 ||
Brahmā spoke to Dakṣa, who was standing near him:
"O Dakṣa, this daughter of yours, being of virtuous vows, will indeed give birth [to a son]. (5022)
Then, having heard the word of Brahmā, Dakṣa, Dharma, and Bhava [produced] four sons, auspicious creators of the four castes. || 5023 ||
Those three, together with Brahmā, mentally took possession of that maiden;
for those who contemplate with truth, the maiden was immediately born.
They were four young princes, equal in appearance;
they were accomplished in their tasks and born endowed with splendor.
And seeing those newborn bodies, which were incapable of enjoyment,
they themselves then understood and spoke with the voice of Brahmā.
Exerting themselves, they indeed pulled [the child], each saying, "My son! My son!
Reflecting upon those who had arisen from their own selves, they spoke thus to one another: || 5027 ||
Whichever son was equal to his father in physical form, let him attend upon that father;
and whichever was likewise similar to him in appearance, prowess, and name. || 5028 ||
Let him take it—may it be well with you—whoever is his equal in appearance;
for a son always conforms to the fixed form of his father. || 5029 ||
Therefore, a son is equal to one's own self for both father and mother by virtue of their seed.
Having thus made this agreement, those of the same caste took sons as wives.

Since the sons of those [progenitors], beginning with Brahmā, were indeed of the same class (savarṇa), and the Manus were of the same class, therefore that state of being of the same class (savarṇatva) exists among them. || 5031 ||
Because they were born from Manas through mental creation, they are remembered as the Manus;
this occurred when the Cākṣuṣa interval had passed and the Vaivasvata interval had arrived.
The son of Prajāpati Ruci was a son named Raucya;
and he who was begotten by Kavi upon Bhūti was the son named Bhautya. || 5033 ||
In the Vaivasvata interval, two Manus were born from Vivasvat:
Manu Vaivasvata and the renowned Sāvarṇa. || 5034 ||
The eldest son of Saṃjñā was the wise lord Manu Vaivasvata;
another son of Savarṇā is also remembered as Manu Vaivasvata. || 5035 ||
And those four Sāvarṇa Manus, born of the great seers,
have indeed perfected their selves through austerity during their respective Manvantaras.
In future times, they will be the accomplishers of all tasks and purposes.
First, I shall proclaim Merusāvarṇi; listen, O sages!
Pārā, Marīcigarbha, and Sudharmā—these three high-souled ones were all born during the Vaivasvata interval. || 5038 ||
These shall be the sons of Rohita, the Prajāpati, who was the son of Dakṣa;
they will be future beings, and each one shall consist of a group of twelve.
Aiśvara, Graha, Rāhu, Vāku, and likewise Vaṃśa—these twelve Pārās are to be known; now learn of the Uttarās: || 5040 ||
Vājīpa, Vājijit, Prabhūti, Kakud, Dadhikrāvā, Vipakva, Praṇita, Vijaya, and Madhu. || 5041 ||
Utathya and Uttama are the two; these twelve are the Marīcis.
Now I shall speak of the Sudharmans; learn their names: || 5042 ||
Varṇa, as well as Athagarvi, Bhuraṇya, Vrajana, Amita, Dravaketu, Jambha, and then Aja is Śakra. || 504 ||
The Sudharmas are proclaimed to be Sunemi and Dyutayas;
their Indra at that time shall be known by the name Adbhuta. || 5044 ||
Skanda is the son of Parvati, while Kartikeya is the son of Agni;
Medhatithi is the descendant of Pulastya, and Vasu is the descendant of Kashyapa;
Jyotishmat is of Bhrigu’s lineage, and likewise Dyumat is of Angiras’s lineage. || 51 ||
Savana, the son of Vasiṣṭha; Havyavāhana, the son of Atri; and Satya, the son of Pulaha—these were the sages during the Rohita Manvantara.
O lord of men, there are exactly three hosts of deities there;
they are the sons of the son of Dakṣa.
Of Rohita Prajāpati. || 521 ||
Dhṛṣṭaketu, Dīptiketu, Pañcahasta, Nirāmaya, Pṛthuśravas, Bhūridyumna,
Rciḥka, Bṛhata, and Gaya. || 53 ||
The first Sāvarṇi had nine sons of great luster. Now, in the tenth cycle, during the interval of the second Manu— (54)
Now, in the tenth period of Manu, the son of Dharma,
the second Sāvarṇi.
In the interval of this very Bhāvya Manu: || 54 ||
Two groups alone are recorded as being opposed to the Sudhāmans:
the Tviṣimantas; and all of them are equal in number, being one hundred each. || 54 ||
The hundred vital breaths (prāṇas) which have been declared by the sages among men—these shall indeed become the gods of Manu Dharmaputra;
their wise Indra shall be known as Śānti. || 54 ||
Haviṣmān the son of Pulaha, Sukṛti the son of Bhṛgu, Āpomūrti the son of Atri, and Vasiṣṭha are remembered as the Apavas. || 55 ||
